name: python-stable_unique
prompt: Write python code implementing a function named stable_unique with parameters values. Return the unique values in their original order. Output only the function code. No example calls, no main program.
checks:
assert stable_unique([]) == []
assert stable_unique([1, 2, 1, 3, 2]) == [1, 2, 3]
assert stable_unique([0, 0]) == [0]

name: python-flatten
prompt: Write python code implementing a function named flatten with parameters rows. Flatten a list of lists by one level. Output only the function code. No example calls, no main program.
checks:
assert flatten([]) == []
assert flatten([[], [1, 2], [], [3]]) == [1, 2, 3]
assert flatten([[0]]) == [0]

name: python-prefix_sums
prompt: Write python code implementing a function named prefix_sums with parameters values. Return cumulative sums, including the current value at each position. Output only the function code. No example calls, no main program.
checks:
assert prefix_sums([]) == []
assert prefix_sums([2, -1, 4]) == [2, 1, 5]
assert prefix_sums([0, 0]) == [0, 0]

name: python-count_words
prompt: Write python code implementing a function named count_words with parameters text. Split on whitespace, lowercase each word, and return a mapping from words to their occurrence counts. Output only the function code. No example calls, no main program.

name: python-is_palindrome
prompt: Write python code implementing a function named is_palindrome with parameters text. Return whether the string is a palindrome after retaining only ASCII letters and digits and lowercasing. Output only the function code. No example calls, no main program.
checks:
assert is_palindrome('') == True
assert is_palindrome('A man, a plan, a canal: Panama!') == True
assert is_palindrome('abc') == False

name: python-gcd
prompt: Write python code implementing a function named gcd with parameters a, b. Return the nonnegative greatest common divisor of two integers. gcd(0,0) is 0. Output only the function code. No example calls, no main program.
checks:
assert gcd(0, 0) == 0
assert gcd(-12, 18) == 6
assert gcd(81, 27) == 27

name: python-chunk
prompt: Write python code implementing a function named chunk with parameters values, size. Split the list into successive lists of size elements; keep a short final list. size is always positive. Output only the function code. No example calls, no main program.

name: python-lower_bound
prompt: Write python code implementing a function named lower_bound with parameters values, target. For a sorted numeric list, return the first index whose value is at least target, or the list length. Output only the function code. No example calls, no main program.
checks:
assert lower_bound([], 5) == 0
assert lower_bound([1, 3, 3, 7], 3) == 1
assert lower_bound([1, 3, 3, 7], 8) == 4
assert lower_bound([1, 3, 3, 7], 0) == 0
